title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscript, where Grothendieck develops a combinatorial or axiomatic theory of 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set of 'figures' carrying two relations: <= (sub-figure) and << (incidence or specialization). It also carries a reflexive, symmetric relation of 'geometric compatibility' (written as a struck-out asymp). Figures can be joined (F v G) when compatible, and each figure F decomposes into 'multistrata' F_A. Fig(L) is the atelier of all set-theoretic figures in a set L.

The previous page proves a Scholium: giving an atelier that is (quasi-)set-theoretic and 'tends to =' is the same as giving a pair (L, F), where F is a sub-atelier of Fig(L) containing every point-figure {{x}} (Axiom*1). L is recovered as the <<-minimal nonempty elements of F.

This page lists the remaining conditions that a subset F of Fig(L) must satisfy:
- Axiom*2 (hereditary): F is closed downward under <=, i.e. every sub-figure of a member of F is in F.
- Axiom*3 (pairwise or local gluing): suppose F, G are in F, and for every multistratum F_A of F and G_B of G the pair {F_A, G_B} is a 'joint' in F. That means F_A and G_B are compatible and F_A v G_B is in F, i.e. F and G are 'multistratally compatible'. Then F v G is in F.

Grothendieck then makes this explicit in terms of local data. Take a set M of elementary figures (multistrata) in L, with a reflexive symmetric relation 'compatible relative to M' (geometric compatibility), satisfying:
- M1: every point-figure {{x}} is in M.
- M2: M is closed under sub-multistrata.
- M3: compatibility relative to M is inherited by sub-figures (X' <= X, Y' <= Y). It also implies compatibility in the ambient Fig(L).

The next page completes the dictionary for figures of finite type. F is recovered as the set of finite-type figures all of whose multistrata lie in M and are pairwise M-compatible. So the atelier is determined by its 'vertices' (multistrata) and a binary compatibility relation, in the manner of a clique (flag) complex. The purpose is to give a concrete, checkable presentation of set-theoretic ateliers, i.e. sub-ateliers of Fig(L), within his axiomatization of 'tame' stratified geometry.
errors: The transcription writes 'F_A ≭ G_A' and 'F_A ∪ G_A'; by the sense (and largely the image) these should be F_A ≭ G_B and F_A ∨ G_B. The manuscript itself shows index slippage here.
Axiom*2 ends 'est dans F' where the script 𝓕 (the class) is meant, not the figure F.

Axiom*3 as stated only gives closure of F under binary joins of multistratally compatible figures. Recovering F from (M, compatibility) on the next page requires a finite-type hypothesis, which Grothendieck adds there. As stated on this page the equivalence is only partial ('partielle' in the margin).

ideas.what: Characterization of set-theoretic sub-ateliers F of Fig(L) by heredity (Axiom*2) and closure under joins of pairwise (multistratally) compatible figures (Axiom*3)
ideas.modern_name: Down-closed family closed under compatible joins; analogous to a flag/clique-complex condition or a 'coherent' family
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; the framework of ateliers is Grothendieck's own (unpublished)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); ateliers do not appear in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Presentation of the atelier by a set M of elementary figures (multistrata) with a reflexive symmetric 'geometric compatibility' relation, hereditary under sub-figures; figures are the compatible families
ideas.modern_name: Coherence-space-like presentation (tokens + reflexive symmetric coherence, cliques); clique complex of a compatibility graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coherence spaces: J.-Y. Girard (1986-87); flag complexes: standard combinatorics

missed.claim: Grothendieck presents ateliers of figures by a set of local pieces M plus a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, closed under sub-objects, with figures as the pairwise-compatible families. Structurally this is Girard's coherence-space / clique presentation (of the same date, 1986-87), here applied to stratified 'tame' geometry. The parallel does not seem to have been noted.
missed.quote: d'un ensemble M de figures élémentaires dans L, relation refl. et sym. ≭_M ("compatibilité géométrique") dans M, satisfaisant les conditions Axiome M1 ... M3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor curiosity rather than a usable result. It suggests the atelier formalism for tame topology is a domain-theoretic or coherence-style structure, which could help anyone trying to reconstruct or formalize the unpublished theory of ateliers.

missed.claim: The theory of ateliers, an axiomatic framework for 'analysis situs' or tame stratified geometry built from figures with relations <=, << and compatibility, remains unpublished and undeveloped. This page is one step: the representation theorem for set-theoretic ateliers.
missed.quote: Axiome* 3 Si F, G ∈ 𝓕, et si pour toute multistrate F_A de F, G_B de G ... F ∨ G ∈ 𝓕
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A worked-out theory could be compared with o-minimal structures and Hrushovski–Loeser style tame-topology formalisms, which partially realize the tame topology programme of the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine axiomatization step, but it belongs to an entirely unpublished framework (ateliers). The coherence-space-like presentation is a mildly interesting structural parallel; the mathematics itself is elementary.
transcription_corrections: 'F_A ≭ G_A et F_A ∪ G_A ∈ 𝓕' should read 'F_A ≭ G_B et F_A ∨ G_B ∈ 𝓕'.
'toute sous figure de F est dans F' should read '... est dans 𝓕'.
'pour reconnaître les conditions' is doubtful; the image suggests something like 'pour énoncer les conditions (de la fig 42) pour qu'une partie 𝓕 de Fig(L) les vérifie'.
In the last line the subscript under the second compatibility sign is not 'm'. It looks like a marker for ambient compatibility (in Fig(L)), so the line reads 'X ≭_M Y ⇒ X ≭ Y'.
The next page's 'Axiom H1 – Axiom H3' should be 'Axiome M1 – M3', and 'x ∈ M' there should be 'X ∈ M'.
